questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I would very much like to try to expand my German language in order to be able to use these skills in the things I wanted to do at KU. At the same time, the German language has also been a general interest of mine, and something had to be done to take it seriously. That's why I wanted to do an exchange in Heidelberg.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very gut. Much is done physically in Germany, so there is always an open office you can come to if you have any questions. Information on where and how has usually been sent in various emails in the past. So it's a good idea to be aware of it and get it in order before you arrive.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There are dedicated Erasmus staff available. In addition, there are introductory days where all of the relavans are reviewed. However, you are also responsible for making all the information useful in the sense that it is all unclear until you try it yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: You need to be lucky to be allocated student accommodation. However, I was lucky to get one, but when I arrived there was mould in the room. It was a basement room and perhaps the last option before it wasn't possible. I was assured that it would be fixed, but anyway I chose to look for another place to live myself because in general the housing administration was quite indifferent. However, I am only speaking from my case worker. Then it took me 1 month to find some private accommodation, which I ended up being happy with.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very difficult to find anything. Start well in advance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: See above. But it was just me who was unlucky. Many were happy with their student accommodation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy. But it just takes a lot of time. Especially in Germany which bureucratically lives 20 years back in time. Everything is done on paper and therefore you always have to print documents, scan documents etc.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You start receiving instructions about six months before. After that, a process starts in which you have to fill in various documents regularly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: When you had questions, you could always write an email to the Erasmus staff. However, you are often redirected or it takes a long time. You have to be proactive and write the same email several times to several people.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I just showed up and asked if I could participate. Otherwise, it is also normal to write an email directly to the teacher with the same request. It was very charming and a plus of the conservative approaches.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and do things at the pace they occur. Although I'm still not convinced it will all work out, enough people say it will.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took both Hauptseminar and Vorlesungen. There is a lot of work to do. Though not as reading-heavy as I've been used to at KU, but it was also very conditional to my Professor Roland Reuß method. So hard to say anything in general, as I'm sure it depends on many things.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more detail-oriented. There was no hurry. Often we spent a week going through half a page. At KU, it was usually 300-400 pages you had to go through.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Hölderlin, Hyperion
Tagebücher - Kafka, Musil, Doderer, Jünger
Lyrik & Edition Vorlesung
Wiederholung - Kierkegaard bis zum Deleuze

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Those you can choose bei Herr. Reuß or Herr. König

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Much more expensive rent due to relocation

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent. And food too. It not like in Berlin or the northern part of Germany. It it really like Denmark in the 'south' of Germany

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not seek them so much. Not in an active a-sociality, just because there were many other things that came naturally too. Through local friends one might be lucky to meet.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Everything between heaven and earth of sport. Even rowing and more 'narrow' sports.
Culturally, I was under the impression that you had to go to Mannheim. In Heidelberg there are not many opportunities. However, a theatre and a concert hall, which were fine. By the way, the theatre is free for students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be with friends and walk in the forrest.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Be with friends and walk in the forrest.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. The people and culture are much like the one we know in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's a difficult balance, but my impression was that it comes if you just show interest and be open minded. But it's hard to give advice on such complex issues.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The politeness and conservatism of the language you should be aware of.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The general openness and unpretentious kind of coziness that can arise in smaller towns like Heidelberg. And the language and literature. And music etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient with all the formalities. There are a lot of them and you will definitely be stressed because you are so often looking for answers to all sorts of questions. Also consider that semester times are staggered, which also makes things and practicalities harder to deal with.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing further.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get an insight into how universities and Germany work and the opportunity to learn the language. They are very proud of all their 'Great'-Geist-personalites. And it's a pleasure to get an insight into, if you're interested

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping calm with all the paperwork and finding a new place to stay after arrival.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
